newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei falls moderately in early morning.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei falls moderately in early morning.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index fell moderately in early trade on Wednesday, erasing small gains posted at the opening.

The weaker yen against the dollar encouraged bargain-hunting in export-driven issues that had been hit recently, but underlying worries about Japan's slow economic recovery weighed on the market, they said.
After 15 minutes of trade, the 225-share Nikkei average had shed 120.21 points or 0.62 percent to trade at 19,394.24. Nikkei September futures fell 90 points to 19,350.

Brokers said the market was also weighed down by penalties against Nomura Securities Co Ltd that take effect on Wednesday. The penalties, for payoffs to a racketeer, include a halt in trading on its own account.

Japan's customs-cleared trade data for the first 20 days of July, released before the market opened, was mostly shrugged off by stock market participants, as the dollar's strength was not hurt by data, brokers said. The surplus rose 126.4 percent from a year earlier to 480.57 billion yen ($4.03 billion) billion) in 20-day period.
The dollar stood at around 119.40 yen in early Tokyo trade.
